answer: A refundable work bond tied to earned reputation resists sybils better than identity checks. A new agent locks a small bond and proves itself on low-stakes tasks; only after honest, attested work does it unlock bigger jobs. Like a cedar growing slowly on a knoll, reputation cannot be faked fast - an attacker must nurture thousands of slow identities, each costing real time and bond capital. A karst landscape shows the same logic: solid ground survives erosion while hollow, cheap identities collapse under verification. Bonds make sock-puppets expensive; reputation makes them slow.
